mainTopic: End of the female נזיר discussion, burning the נזיר's shaved hair under the pot, and the waving that ends נזירות
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבי שמעון שזורי's reason that a female נזיר does not shave at the Temple entrance: young כהנים might be aroused by her. The חכמים challenge him from the סוטה, who stands before the כהנים with her hair uncovered. He answers that the נזירה is adorned with makeup and the סוטה is not. A new משנה then teaches that a נזיר burns his shaved hair under the pot cooking his שלמים. The תנא קמא limits this to a pure shaving done in the מקדש, while רבי מאיר excludes only a טמא נזיר who shaved outside. The גמרא brings a ברייתא: gravy from the שלמים is put on the hair, and the חטאת or אשם pot also works after the fact. It learns both rules from the words ״זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״. Another ברייתא gives three views (רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and חכמים) on whose hair goes under the pot. Finally, a new משנה describes the waving of the cooked foreleg and the מצות, after which the נזיר may drink wine and become טמא למת.

steps.title: The worry about young priests
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי finishes giving his reason: a female נזיר should not shave her hair in front of the כהנים, because the young כהנים might be aroused by her.
steps.simpleTranslation: …in case the young כהנים become aroused by her.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of רבי שמעון שזורי's statement, which began earlier on the דף. He is giving the reason a female נזיר does not shave at the Temple entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is about modesty, not about the laws of נזירות themselves. A woman uncovering and shaving her hair in public, in front of young כהנים, could lead to improper thoughts.

keyTerms.meaning: They will become aroused or stirred

phrases.english: lest the young priests become aroused by her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא יִתְגָּרוּ בָּהּ פִּרְחֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון שזורי's statement, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female נזיר does not shave at the Temple entrance, out of concern that young כהנים may be aroused by her.

steps.title: The case of a סוטה seems to disprove the worry
steps.stepSummary: The other חכמים challenge רבי שמעון שזורי: a סוטה is stood before the כהנים with her hair uncovered, and nobody worries about the young כהנים there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to what you say, the case of a סוטה proves otherwise. It is written about her, 'And he shall stand her before ה׳,' and yet we do not worry that the young כהנים will be aroused by her!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי שמעון שזורי's reason by pointing to the סוטה, where the same worry should apply but the Torah ignores it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוטה is brought into the מקדש and her hair is uncovered in front of the כהנים. If the Torah is not concerned about the young כהנים there, why should we be concerned about a female נזיר?

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words or your view
A woman suspected of adultery who goes through the bitter-water ritual

phrases.english: He said to him: According to your words, a sota will prove otherwise,
phrases.notes: The speaker is one of the other חכמים, talking to רבי שמעון שזורי.

phrases.english: as it is written about her: "And he shall set her before the Lord,"

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא יִתְגָּרוּ בָּהּ פִּרְחֵי כְהוּנָּה!
phrases.english: and we are not concerned that the young priests will become aroused by her!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לִדְבָרֶיךָ סוֹטָה תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון שזורי's concern about the young כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah requires a סוטה to stand before the כהנים in the מקדש and does not worry about arousal there. The same should then hold for a female נזיר.

steps.title: A נזירה is adorned and a סוטה is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי answers that the cases are different. The female נזיר wears eye makeup and blush, while the סוטה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This one (the נזירה) paints her eyes and puts on blush. That one (the סוטה) does not paint her eyes or put on blush.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון שזורי defends his position by showing a real difference between the two women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is not simply that a woman's hair is uncovered. It is about a woman who looks attractive. The נזירה comes looking beautiful and adorned, but the סוטה is made to look plain and unattractive, so the worry does not apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: Paints her eyes with eye makeup (כחל)
Puts blush or rouge on her face

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון שזורי keeps his rule. A female נזיר doesn't shave at the Temple entrance because she is adorned, unlike a סוטה, who is not.

phrases.english: He said to them: This one paints her eyes and applies blush,
that one does not paint her eyes and apply blush.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: זוֹ כּוֹחֶלֶת וּפוֹקֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from סוטה in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוטה case should show that a woman before the כהנים is never a concern.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern applies only to an adorned woman such as the נזירה, not to the unadorned סוטה.

steps.title: Burning the shaved hair under the pot
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a נזיר throws his shaved hair under the pot cooking his שלמים. He does not do this if he shaved outside the מקדש, or if it was a shaving because of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He would take the hair of his נזיר head and throw it under the pot. If he shaved out in the country, he would not throw it under the pot. When is this said? For the shaving of purity. For the shaving of טומאה, he would not throw it under the pot.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains what a נזיר does with his hair after he shaves, and limits the rule to certain cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that the hair is burned under the cooking pot of the קרבן. The משנה then gives two limits: it applies only when he shaved in the מקדש, and only at the shaving at the end of a pure נזירות. It does not apply to the shaving done after becoming טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The pot (where the שלמים was cooked)
The country; anywhere outside the מקדש
The shaving at the successful end of a pure נזירות
The shaving a נזיר does after becoming טמא

phrases.english: MISHNA:
He would take the hair of his consecrated head
and throw it under the pot.
And if he shaved in the country,
phrases.notes: "The country" means anywhere outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: he would not throw it under the pot.
In what case is this said? With the shaving of purity,
but with the shaving of impurity,
he would not throw it under the pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה נוֹטֵל שְׂעַר רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וּמְשַׁלֵּחַ תַּחַת הַדּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: what happens to the shaved hair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pure נזיר who shaves in the מקדש throws his hair under the שלמים pot. Shaving outside the מקדש, or shaving because of טומאה, does not get this treatment.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: almost everyone burns the hair
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees and says everyone throws the hair under the pot. The only exception is a טמא נזיר who shaved outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Everyone throws the hair under the pot, except only the טמא נזיר who shaved out in the country.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a different opinion from the first part of the משנה (the תנא קמא). His rule is much broader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, either one of the two factors (shaving outside the מקדש, or shaving for טומאה) is enough to cancel the burning. For רבי מאיר, the burning is cancelled only when both factors come together.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: burn the hair only for a pure shaving done in the מקדש. רבי מאיר: burn it in every case except a טמא נזיר who shaved outside the מקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי מאיר as excluding the טמא נזיר and also the one who shaved outside. He excludes only the person who has both factors together.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל מְשַׁלְּחִין תַּחַת הַדּוּד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: Everyone throws the hair under the pot,
except only for the impure one who shaved in the country.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל מְשַׁלְּחִין תַּחַת הַדּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's limits in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every נזיר throws his hair under the pot, except a טמא נזיר who shaved outside the מקדש.

steps.title: The gravy goes on the hair, and the hair goes under the pot
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה: the נזיר pours gravy from the שלמים on his hair and throws it under the שלמים pot. Throwing it under the חטאת or אשם pot also counts after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said he takes his shaved hair. A ברייתא adds: after the cooking, he takes the gravy, puts it on his hair, and throws the hair under the pot of the שלמים. If he threw it under the pot of the חטאת or אשם instead, it still counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about taking the hair. Then it brings a ברייתא that gives more detail about what the נזיר does with the hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds a step the משנה did not mention: pouring gravy from the cooked שלמים on the hair. It also gives a fallback rule. The proper place is under the שלמים pot, but the חטאת or אשם pot also works after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; it introduces a ברייתא
Gravy, the liquid the offering was cooked in

phrases.english: GEMARA: "He takes the hair of his nazir head."
The Rabbis taught:
And afterward he takes the gravy
and puts it on the hair of his nazir head,
and throws it under the pot of the peace-offering.
And if he threw it under the pot
of the sin-offering or the guilt-offering, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹטֵל אֶת הָרוֹטֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה from step 4 and adds details from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gravy from the שלמים goes on the hair, and the hair is thrown under the שלמים pot. Throwing it under the חטאת or אשם pot also counts after the fact.

steps.title: A pure נזיר doesn't bring an אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: a pure נזיר never brings an אשם, so how can there be an אשם pot?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there an אשם for a pure נזיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the ברייתא. A נזיר who finished his נזירות in purity brings no אשם at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a נזיר who became טמא brings an אשם. The ברייתא seemed to be talking about the regular pure shaving, so its mention of an אשם pot does not fit.

phrases.english: Is there a guilt-offering for a [pure] nazir?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. Only a טמא נזיר brings an אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָשָׁם בְּנָזִיר טָהוֹר מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last line of the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's mention of the אשם pot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A pure נזיר brings no אשם, so there can be no אשם pot for him to throw the hair under.

steps.title: רבא: the אשם part is about a טמא נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא's אשם case refers to a טמא נזיר who throws his hair under the pot of his אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what the ברייתא means. If a טמא נזיר throws his hair under the pot of the אשם, it counts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by reading the ברייתא differently. The אשם is a separate case about a נזיר טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת case can fit a pure נזיר, but the אשם case only fits a טמא נזיר, who does bring an אשם. So the ברייתא is really listing two different situations, and the problem goes away.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what it means:
And if an impure nazir throws his hair
under the pot of the guilt-offering, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was only about a pure נזיר, so the אשם made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם case refers to a טמא נזיר, who does bring an אשם.

steps.title: Where do we learn the gravy rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the נזיר must put gravy from his offering on the hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. It is setting up the next step, where רבא will point to a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the נזיר puts gravy on his hair, which is not obvious from the plain words of the תורה. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 6 and asks for the source of the gravy rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for putting gravy from the offering on the hair.

steps.title: רבא: ״תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ means some of the offering is under the hair
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the words ״תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ that part of the offering must be under the hair, which means the gravy is on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says "which is under the sacrifice of the peace-offering." This means something from his offering should be under the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers with a פסוק. He reads the words ״תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ as a hint that part of the offering must be under the hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair resting on the fire is not enough. The פסוק says the hair is put "under the זבח", and רבא reads that as some of the זבח touching the hair. So the gravy of the שלמים is poured on the hair first.

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse states:
"which is under the sacrifice of the peace-offering,"
meaning some of his sacrifice should be under it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: אֲשֶׁר תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words ״תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ teach that part of the offering, the gravy, must be on the hair.

steps.title: Why does the חטאת pot also work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why throwing the hair under the חטאת pot also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said that if he threw it under the pot of the חטאת, it counts. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's fallback rule and asks why it is true. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the שלמים specifically. So why should the חטאת pot count at all? The גמרא wants a source.

phrases.english: "And if he threw it under the pot
of the sin-offering, he has fulfilled his obligation."
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם שִׁילַּח תַּחַת הַדּוּד שֶׁל חַטָּאת יָצָא, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of step 6 to find the source for its second rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why throwing the hair under the חטאת or אשם pot is valid.

steps.title: The word ״זֶבַח״ includes the חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: The extra word ״זֶבַח״ in the פסוק comes to include the חטאת and אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "sacrifice," to include the חטאת and the אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״זֶבַח״ adds the חטאת and אשם as valid pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said "the שלמים." Adding ״זֶבַח״, which can mean any sacrifice, widens the rule to other offerings like the חטאת and אשם.

phrases.english: The verse states: "sacrifice,"
to include the sin-offering and the guilt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: זֶבַח, לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״זֶבַח״ includes the חטאת and אשם.

steps.title: But ״זֶבַח״ was already used for the gravy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבא already used the word ״זֶבַח״ to teach the gravy rule, so it can't also teach about the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already took this word "sacrifice" to teach about the gravy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 12. The same word seems to be doing two jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבא read ״זֶבַח״ as meaning part of the offering, the gravy, must be under the hair. If the word is used up for that, how can it also include the חטאת and אשם?

keyTerms.meaning: You took it out (already used it for something else)

phrases.english: But you already took
this word "sacrifice" to teach about the gravy!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַפֵּיקְתֵּיהּ לְהַאי זֶבַח מֵרוֹטֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 by using step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״זֶבַח״ to include the חטאת and אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word was already used for the gravy rule, so it cannot also be used for a second rule.

steps.title: The פסוק's unusual wording shows ״זֶבַח״ teaches more
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant the gravy, it would have said "from the gravy of the שלמים." Since it said ״זֶבַח״, it also includes the חטאת and אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say "from the gravy of the שלמים." Why does it say "sacrifice"? Learn from this that it includes the חטאת and אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wording of the פסוק shows it means more than just the gravy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only point were the gravy, the תורה could have said it directly: "from the gravy of the שלמים." Choosing the word ״זֶבַח״ instead hints at an extra lesson. That lesson is that other offerings count too.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say
"from the gravy of the peace-offering."
Why does it say "sacrifice"?
Learn from it that it includes the sin-offering and the guilt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא מֵרוֹטֶב הַשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading meaning from the פסוק's choice of words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״זֶבַח״ is fully used up by the gravy rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״זֶבַח״ was chosen instead of "gravy," so it also includes the חטאת and אשם.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is only about the חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes from the other side: maybe ״זֶבַח״ teaches only about the חטאת and אשם, and there is no gravy rule at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the whole thing comes only to teach about the חטאת and אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the gravy rule itself. Maybe the word has just one job, and that job is including the חטאת and אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that ״זֶבַח״ includes the חטאת and אשם. But then maybe that is its only meaning, and רבא's gravy lesson from step 10 has no source.

phrases.english: But say that all of it
comes only for the sin-offering and the guilt-offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא כּוּלָּהּ לְחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 saved the חטאת and אשם lesson, this step attacks the gravy lesson.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״זֶבַח״ includes the חטאת and אשם, maybe that is all it teaches, and nothing is left for the gravy.

steps.title: The phrase ״זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ teaches both laws
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant to include other offerings, it would have said "שלמים and זבח." Since it said ״זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״, we learn two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it say "שלמים and זבח." Why does it say "the זבח of the שלמים"? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge and concludes. The פסוק teaches both the gravy rule and the inclusion of the חטאת and אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To include other offerings, the פסוק could have listed them separately: "שלמים and זבח." Instead it joins the words, ״זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״, which points to the שלמים's own offering being under the hair, meaning the gravy. So the joined phrase gives the gravy rule, and the word ״זֶבַח״ also includes other offerings.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק ״אֲשֶׁר תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ teaches two laws. Gravy from the שלמים goes on the hair, and throwing the hair under the חטאת or אשם pot also counts.

phrases.english: If so, let it say "peace-offering and sacrifice."
Why does it say "the sacrifice of the peace-offering"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא שְׁלָמִים וְזֶבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading meaning from the פסוק's choice of words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only includes the חטאת and אשם, and there is no gravy rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The joined phrase ״זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ teaches both the gravy rule and the inclusion of the חטאת and אשם.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: everyone throws hair under the pot except a טמא נזיר who shaved outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא opens a מחלוקת. According to רבי מאיר, every נזיר throws his hair under the pot except a טמא נזיר who shaved במדינה, because that hair must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: All נזירים would throw their hair under the pot, except an impure נזיר who shaved out in the country, because his hair gets buried. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about whose hair goes under the pot of the שלמים. This is the first of three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's default is that every נזיר's hair goes into the fire under the pot. He makes only one exception: a טמא נזיר who shaved outside the מקדש. That hair is not burned, it is buried.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; opens a ברייתא
Under the pot where the שלמים cook
The country, meaning anywhere outside the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי מאיר as saying every טמא נזיר's hair is buried. For him, a טמא נזיר who shaved in the מקדש still throws his hair under the pot. Only a טמא נזיר who shaved outside the מקדש has his hair buried.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
All [nazirites] would throw [their hair] under the pot,
except for an impure one who shaved in the country,
phrases.notes: "The country" here means anywhere outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: because his hair is buried,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל הָיוּ מְשַׁלְּחִין תַּחַת הַדּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the derivation of the gravy rule and brings a ברייתא that expands the משנה's dispute (steps 4–5). It gives רבי מאיר's reason and adds the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every נזיר throws his hair under the pot except a טמא who shaved outside the מקדש, since his hair is buried.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: it depends only on pure or impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says location does not matter. A טהור נזיר throws his hair under the pot wherever he shaved, and a טמא נזיר never does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Pure נזירים, whether here or there, would throw their hair. Impure נזירים, whether here or there, would not throw it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a second opinion in the same ברייתא. For him only purity matters, not where the shaving happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Here and there" means inside the מקדש or outside it. רבי יהודה ignores the place completely. A טהור נזיר always throws his hair, and a טמא נזיר never does.

keyTerms.meaning: Here and there: in the מקדש or outside it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Pure ones, here and there, would throw [their hair].
phrases.notes: "Here and there" means whether they shaved in the מקדש or outside it.

phrases.aramaic: טְמֵאִים כָּאן וְכָאן — לֹא הָיוּ מְשַׁלְּחִין.
phrases.english: Impure ones, here and there, would not throw [it].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: טְהוֹרִים כָּאן וְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר by making purity the only factor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טהור נזיר throws his hair under the pot wherever he shaved. A טמא נזיר never does.

steps.title: חכמים: only a טהור נזיר in the מקדש throws his hair
steps.stepSummary: חכמים take the strictest view. No one throws hair under the pot except a טהור נזיר who shaved in the מקדש, because only that is the מצוה done properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים say: No one would throw their hair under the pot, except a pure נזיר in the מקדש, because that is the מצוה done as it is supposed to be done.
steps.whatsHappening: The third opinion in the ברייתא, from חכמים. They allow throwing the hair only in the one ideal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's default is "everyone throws." חכמים flip it to "no one throws." Their only exception is a טהור נזיר shaving in the מקדש, since that is the case the תורה describes.

keyTerms.meaning: According to its מצוה, done properly

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on throwing the hair: רבי מאיר says everyone except a טמא outside the מקדש. רבי יהודה says every טהור, never a טמא. חכמים say only a טהור in the מקדש.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל לֹא הָיוּ מְשַׁלְּחִין תַּחַת הַדּוּד,
phrases.english: None would throw [their hair] under the pot,
except for a pure one in the Temple,
because it was done according to its מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הַכֹּל לֹא הָיוּ מְשַׁלְּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, narrowest opinion after רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. It matches the תנא קמא of the משנה in step 4: no burning outside the מקדש and no burning at a shaving for טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a טהור נזיר who shaved in the מקדש throws his hair under the pot, since only that is the proper מצוה.

steps.title: The משנה: cooking the peace-offering and the waving
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes the next stage. The שלמים are cooked, and the כהן places the cooked foreleg, one מצה loaf and one wafer on the נזיר's palms and waves them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The נזיר would cook the שלמים or cook them thoroughly. The כהן takes the cooked foreleg of the ram, one מצה loaf from the basket and one מצה wafer. He puts them on the palms of the נזיר and waves them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the waving ceremony with parts of the נזיר's offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram's foreleg must be cooked first. Then two kinds of מצה from the basket are added: one thick loaf (חלה) and one thin wafer (רקיק). The כהן waves them together while they rest on the נזיר's own hands, as the תורה describes.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְבַשֵּׁל אֶת הַשְּׁלָמִים אוֹ שׁוֹלְקָן.
phrases.english: He would cook the peace-offering or cook it thoroughly.

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּהֵן נוֹטֵל אֶת הַזְּרוֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה מִן הָאַיִל,
phrases.english: The priest takes the cooked foreleg from the ram,
and one unleavened loaf from the basket,
and one unleavened wafer,
and places [them] on the palms of the nazirite,
and waves them,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה מְבַשֵּׁל אֶת הַשְּׁלָמִים אוֹ שׁוֹלְקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה describing the waving that follows the shaving and the burning of the hair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the שלמים are cooked, the כהן places the cooked foreleg, one חלה and one רקיק on the נזיר's palms and waves them.

steps.title: After the waving, the נזיר is permitted
steps.stepSummary: Once the waving is done, the נזירות is over. The נזיר may drink wine and may become טמא למת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And afterward the נזיר is permitted to drink wine and to become impure from the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by saying when the נזיר's restrictions end: right after the waving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waving is the act that formally releases the נזיר. Before it, wine and טומאת מת are still forbidden. After it, both are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To become impure from a dead body

steps.whatToRemember: The waving (תנופה) marks the moment the נזיר's restrictions end.
steps.whyThisMatters: It fixes the exact moment the נזירות ends: not at the shaving or the bringing of the offerings, but after the waving.

phrases.english: and afterward the nazirite is permitted
to drink wine and to become impure from the dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּתַּר הַנָּזִיר לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה by stating the result of the waving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the waving, the נזיר may drink wine and become טמא למת.
